english: The son heard the thunder and was afraid. He asked his father why Dyeus thunders (makes thunder). The father said: Perkwunos strikes the serpent with a stone. Water comes down and the god strikes it down. Do not fear after (it). Now it rained and the son listened. The fields are yellow-green in spring. He did not fear and slept.

Father Dyeus saw the beast in the deep, in the sea. It had swallowed the clouds, and on the earth it did not rain. Then he hurled the great stone down. It sank into the sea and the water boiled. It struck the beast which lay there. Its body split and the clouds came out. Then it rained and the streams filled. The pasture grew and the sheep ate it. Afterwards men saw the stone. They set it up as/for a god and honoured it.

The god went out of the mountain in spring. He saw the serpent on the high rock. He slew it; he struck it with the stone. Its red blood flowed onto the rocks. The water was released and the earth drank it. Great fame, imperishable fame, came to the god. The young men sing to him at the feast and the old men bowed.

Perkwunos, you, strong god, we praise. You slew the enemy, the serpent, with the rock. You who scattered the waters, come to us. You who split the rock, give us strength. Your fame among men is imperishable. Now your victory is ... and your eye bright. Hear our song and be dear to us.

The child asked the grandfather: who slew the serpent? The old man said: the god of thunder himself slew it. He struck it with a stone from the sky. Why did he strike it? It shut up the water and the men were thirsty. Its teeth were long and its two eyes were red. Now the water flows and we drink. The child laughed and ran home.

The serpent lay around the waters. The gods saw it and feared it. They fled up under the sky and hid in the clouds. Only the god of thunder dared. The god (h1éymos?) said: do not fear. I will slay the serpent. He went there and struck it three times with the stone. Its tail trembled and it died. The gods came down and stood around the corpse. They praised him who had dared.
uncertain: moréyōh2 read as future/subj 'I will kill'
